title: Level 2 (Intermediate) - D-14
notes:
West leads the ♦K against 4♥. West's ♦K holds the first trick and he continues with the ♦A and the ♦J for South to ruff as East follows. South continues with a winning heart finesse and repeats the finesse as East discards. South draws the last trump and plays 3 rounds of clubs for a spade discard, West following twice.

Dummy's last club is ruffed in the closed hand leaving South in a position where he must play spades for 1 loser in order to make the contract. On the actual layout, West has the ♠Q and East has the ♠A so that South must lead a spade to dummy's ♠J in order to succeed. If the spade honors are reversed, however, South must play a spade to the ♠K (instead of the ♠J).

By the time that South has to make this decision he should know that West cannot hold the ♠A. West is known to have a balanced hand with 12 HCP outside of spades. If West was also dealt the ♠A, as above, he would have opened the bidding with 1NT instead of 1♦. It is possible that West was dealt the ♠Q, so South should play the ♠J if West follows with a low spade on the first round of the suit.
